ratings_why.fun: Lots of cards that bend each other: Berus killing Encore units on purpose, Anguis stealing a Matron's scene, Coronella turning sales into Death Scenes, Old Crest placed to die last; placement decides every turn.
ratings_why.distinct: Death Scene plus Encore is deathrattle plus reborn from Battlegrounds; Understudy, Notices from any tribe's deaths, and the self-harm cards are what lift it above a generic undead tribe.

verdict_why: Two wording gaps (which unit is 'behind', and how Old Crest works with the Prompter and Hesketh) need fixing; the engine itself should stay as it is.

points.text: A front-row Bit-Part Lizard has two units behind it, and a back-row one has none. Say which one gets the buff, for example the one with Understudy first, otherwise random.
Old Crest in front of the Prompter's Boy: does his own Death Scene fire twice, giving two replay passes? And when Sir Hesketh raises him and he dies again, does he replay everything again? Say both.
Give the Tail a tiny Death Scene, such as 'Little Anguis gains +1/+1 permanently'. Then Mr Grey and the Brothers Berus have a reason to kill it, and the joke about better notices pays off.
Let Toad Claque also cheer a unit that steps in. That ties the wings build to the Encore wall instead of keeping them as separate builds.
Mr Grey always destroying your smallest unit is a fun puzzle, since you set up a Tail, Hatchling or Encore unit as his victim. Keep it forced; that is the whole decision.

standouts.why: Copies the dead lead's Death Scene, leaves a body, and counts for the Prompter's Boy: three engines meet in one card.
Selling as a death links the shop to Death Scenes and to Birds' Fly South, a use nobody else planned.
Hurts its own neighbours on purpose, so Encore units trade a life for +4 Attack and a Notice.

weakest.why: One job: steps in and grows itself. Nothing else reads it except the Bit-Part Lizard.
A passive read of Notices with no placement or timing choice.
Four Notices a fight is easy to reach, so it is just a gold piece with no decision.

flags.note: +1/+1 per 2 Notices on a game-long total that never resets, and it swings with lobbies that have Eggs and Oozes.
Doubling while recruiting, with the Rehearser and Coronella, makes a strong shop loop on Dame Natrix.
'A unit behind this' doesn't say which of two diagonals.
His interaction with the Prompter's Boy on his own scene, and with Hesketh's second round, is not stated.
